$comment: The CLOSED set of STATELESS PROTOCOL ADAPTERS this repository may publish.
`release-adapter.yml` resolves its target here through
`scripts/release_adapter.py resolve` and fails closed, so adding a
publishable adapter is a reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time string —
the same doctrine as `.github/release-modules.json`, applied to the other
shape.
## Why this is a SECOND file rather than optional fields in the first
ADR-0006's 2026-08-14 amendment added `stateless-protocol-adapter` for a
distribution a product CALLS rather than installs: no `ModuleManifest`, no
migration lineage, no `MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER` allocation, no persistence
import. Every fact the module lane asserts is therefore absent — a
`db_schema` to compare against the manifest, a `manifest_attr` to register
through `NamespaceRegistry`, a `kernel_floor` naming the release that
allocated the schema.
Making those three OPTIONAL in the module lane would have been the cheaper
diff and the worse one. `resolve` and `verify-wheel` would then accept an
entry with no schema for EVERY module, so a stateful module whose
`db_schema` was dropped in a bad merge would stop being refused and start
being treated as an adapter — the namespace assertion silently skipped
instead of failed. This repository has already recorded that argument once,
about the kernel: 'one workflow pretending to cover both would have to
weaken whichever check the other cannot satisfy'.
So the stateful lane keeps all three fields MANDATORY, and this lane
declares none of them. `scripts/release_adapter.py` REFUSES an entry that
carries `db_schema`, `manifest_attr` or `kernel_floor`: a package with those
facts is a module and belongs in the other file, where the namespace gates
will actually ask it questions.
## The classification is checked, not trusted
`resolve` reads the package's `EXTRACTION.toml` and refuses anything whose
`classification` is not `stateless-protocol-adapter`. That is what stops
this lane from becoming a way to publish a stateful module while skipping
the namespace, lineage and dual-plane checks the module lane performs. The
classification itself is governed generically by
`stateless_adapter_violations` in
`tests/architecture/test_product_first_extraction.py` — four properties, not
a label.
## No composition check, and that is not a gap
The module lane's level-2 check installs a set of modules beside one kernel
and constructs a `NamespaceRegistry`, because two modules that each register
alone can still collide on a schema, a migration prefix or a table. An
adapter owns none of those, so there is nothing for it to contest and a
composition check over it would be theatre. Its verification is the
PUBLIC SURFACE, proved against the installed bytes: every name in `__all__`
importable, the version it reports, and the classification's own
properties — no `ModuleManifest`, no ORM in `sys.modules` after import.
## Why it is empty
`dotmac-auth-oidc 0.1.0a1` is merged, dossier-complete and deliberately NOT
listed. ABSENCE IS THE SAFETY MECHANISM — the same rule ADR-0026 section 8
set for `dotmac-approvals` and ADR-0017 states generally: the release entry
lands with the proof, never ahead of it. The proof owed here is a real pilot
consumer. `dotmac_workspace` must wire `start_login`/`complete_login`
against an EXACT-SHA local wheel (the procedure is in
`packages/dotmac-auth-oidc/README.md` § 'Testing against an unpublished
wheel') and supply a SHARED, ATOMIC `StateStore`, because
`InMemoryStateStore` cannot complete a login started on another worker.
Until that pilot is green this lane resolves nothing and a dispatch fails at
the gate.
Listing an adapter is one reviewed diff: an entry here, plus the workflow's
`choice` options, which `tests/architecture/test_adapter_release_lane.py`
requires to match exactly once this object is non-empty. Publication is
still not adoption — `EXTRACTION.toml`'s `status` and `contract_consumers`
count CONSUMERS, and a release moves neither.
The fleet's OIDC relying party (ADR-0006's 2026-08-14 stateless-protocol-adapter amendment).
LISTED NOW BECAUSE THE PILOT RAN. This lane was built shut in PR #180 and the
reason was explicit: absence from this file is the safety mechanism until a real
consumer wires start_login/complete_login and supplies a SHARED, ATOMIC StateStore.
dotmac_workspace PR #2 is that consumer. It runs the ceremony against its own
PostgreSQL table whose take() is one DELETE ... RETURNING, proven under real
concurrency in tests/db/test_state_store_atomicity.py, and it binds the callback to
the browser with a host-only cookie compared against the query state.
The pilot also CHANGED the package rather than merely consuming it (PR #194): a
database-backed store belongs to one request's transaction, so the store is supplied
per ceremony operation while the client keeps its ProviderCache. Publishing before
that seam existed would have shipped a surface no honest consumer could use.
NO db_schema, manifest_attr or kernel_floor, and their absence is checked rather
than assumed: scripts/release_adapter.py refuses an entry carrying any of them.
This package has no ModuleManifest, no lineage and no ledger allocation, and it does
not depend on dotmac-kernel at all -- a kernel floor would be a fact about a
relationship that does not exist.
Required wheel contents, each earning its place rather than listing the directory:
client.py    -- the flow, the algorithm allowlist and the state-pair check
state.py     -- the StateStore contract, S256 PKCE, the per-request sentinel
discovery.py -- metadata and JWKS with TTLs and rate-limited kid refetch
transport.py -- the one place this package touches a network, redirects refused
errors.py    -- the taxonomy whose subclass names are the stable reason codes
A wheel missing any of them is not a smaller adapter; it is one whose security core
was dropped, and import alone would not always say so.
allowed_requires is pyjwt and httpx: signature verification and network I/O, the two
concerns ADR-0006 says cannot be faked. python-jose is deliberately absent -- see
COMPATIBILITY.md for why the fleet's 3.3.0 pin was not inherited.
Publication is not adoption. EXTRACTION.toml's status stays audit-complete and
contract_consumers stays empty until Workspace PR #2 merges against the published
wheel; a release moves neither.
